description: The pie chart represents the distribution of mathematical topics in a dataset, comparing the proportions of different areas of mathematics. The chart is divided into 11 slices, each representing a distinct topic. The slices are labeled with their corresponding topics and percentages, and are colored differently to distinguish between them. The largest slice, representing "Algebra", is dark blue and accounts for approximately 21.19% of the total, although its label and percentage are presented outside the chart in a legend-like format. The other slices represent "Algebra - High School" (pink, 17.83%), "Pre-Calculus - High School" (brown, 14.21%), "Combinatorics - Olympiad-level" (green, 9.56%), "Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra - University-level" (purple, 6.46%), "Geometry - Olympiad-level" (orange, 6.46%), "Calculus and Analysis - University-level" (light blue, 6.20%), "Probability - University-level" (yellow, 5.43%), "Statistics - University-level" (gray, 4.39%), "Differential Equations - University-level" (teal, 3.62%), and "Geometry - High School" (lavender, 3.62%), with "Number Theory - Olympiad-level" being the smallest slice (peach, 1.03%). The chart does not visually emphasize any particular slice, and the slices are not ordered in a specific way. The percentage labels are shown next to each slice's label outside the chart.
